name: SerialXML
workload: Struct-to-XML serialization of an Order object (nested Address, vector<LineItem>, vector<int> tags) via to_xml(), 100,000 iterations single-threaded, compared against Boost.Serialization's xml_oarchive, cereal's XMLOutputArchive, and pugixml
claimed_speedup: 822.085 ns/iter for SerialXML vs 7899.305 ns/iter for Boost.Serialization (~9.6x, derived from page data) and 7945.590 ns/iter for Cereal (~9.7x, derived from page data); README prose separately claims '8.3x faster than boost_xml' and '1.9x faster than pugixml', which does not match the table's own numbers for the Boost.Serialization row
compiler_and_flags: GCC 16.1 (minimum required for C++26 reflection support); built via CMake 'release-gcc' preset (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, exact optimization flags not enumerated in README or benchmark CMakeLists.txt)
hardware: Single Intel Core 7 240H laptop CPU, 5600 MT/s DDR5 (per README; no further CPU/RAM/OS detail given)
tradeoffs: Requires C++26 with an experimental reflection-capable compiler (GCC 16.1+); XML-only serializer (no binary/JSON formats); annotation-driven API (C++26 struct/member annotations) rather than archive-based like Boost.Serialization/cereal; no versioning/schema-evolution support shown; benchmark payload is small/fixed and not representative of all workloads
caveats: First-party, single-machine, single-run benchmark; optimizer flags not explicitly stated beyond CMake 'Release' build type, so methodology is only partially documented (capped below tier A per rules); the README's prose speedup claim (8.3x vs 'boost_xml') does not match the derived ratio from its own table (~9.6x vs the Boost.Serialization row), an unexplained inconsistency; project has 0 stars and was created only days before this search, and depends on not-yet-stable C++26 reflection compiler support, so real-world adoption/robustness is unproven
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos --topic serialization --language "C++" --sort updated --limit 50, then opened EJainDev/SerialXML and its benchmarks/ directory (xml_serialization_benchmarks.cpp, CMakeLists.txt) to confirm the Boost::serialization and cereal::cereal comparison is real, linked, and buildable
